findings.finding: Leidos is the parent of QTC, the largest VA medical disability exam (MDE) vendor, and is under the same VA incentive pause as MMS's VES unit. On its 2026-11-03 Q3 call it said 'it's highly likely our existing contracts will be extended through the first half of 2027'. Its CFO said the no-incentive Q4 Health exit margin (high teens) 'is a good place to model out the first half of next year', and that ''27 is not a bottom line growth year'. The final recompete RFP had still not been issued; award is expected April-May 2027 and new work July 1, 2027. MMS last spoke on 2026-08-06, when it assumed the pause runs to 2026-12-31 and called Q4 FY26 (about $1.91 adj EPS, about 13% adj EBITDA margin) 'a reasonable run rate for this period'. If MMS guides FY27 the way Leidos does, Q1-Q3 FY27 (Oct 2026-Jun 2027) carry no VA incentives. FY27 then starts from about $7.64 annualized (4 x $1.91) before buybacks and Agile Defense, against FY27 street figures of about $8.4-9.1, a bar that is not verified.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The VA incentive removal and guide cut on 2026-08-06 moved the stock -7.63%. The FY26 revenue guide below consensus on 2026-02-05 moved it -16.51% despite an EPS beat and a raised EPS guide. The strong FY26 guide on 2025-11-20 moved it +5.53%. This name trades on the forward guide, especially revenue, more than on the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is up about 14% since the August print (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-11). Two-analyst FY27 numbers sit above the 4 x Q4 run-rate. If the market had priced a full-1H-2027 no-incentive case off the Leidos call, the post-August rally would have reversed after 2026-11-03, and FY27 figures would have converged toward about $7.6-8.0 ex-Agile. Neither is visible. On thin coverage, a peer read-through is the kind of item that is not mechanically fed into MMS estimates.
findings.independence: Separate source, MMS's own Q3 call (2026-08-06, https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504): management said a contract extension of up to six months is possible and the draft PWS contains no pricing or incentive language. The SAM-search news item of 2026-11-03 (https://samsearch.co/government-contracting-news/vba-disability-exam-recompete-targets-november-rfp-and-2027-start-239915) gives the same RFP and award timeline, but it relays Leidos, so it is not fully independent. Counterweight: Leidos's Q2 CEO comment called the pause '2026-only', which would mean incentives return in the extension; its newer Q3 CFO guidance models 1H27 without them.

findings.finding: MMS's own Q3 FY26 documents: trailing-12-month book-to-bill about 0.5x ($1.25B YTD signed awards), and 'certain opportunities have experienced procurement delays, scope revisions or in some cases, cancellation'. Q3 revenue was $1.28B, down about 5% y/y, with FY26 revenue guided to the low end of $5.20-5.35B. On the other side, $1.35B awarded-but-unsigned, mostly recompetes, and a $50.4B pipeline. Organic FY27 revenue growth guidance is therefore at risk of landing below the high-single-digit FY27 growth an analyst cited on the call. On 2026-11-03 Leidos also flagged 'delays in some decisions' tempering momentum into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY revenue outlook below consensus on 2026-02-05 moved it -16.51%. This is the line the stock punished hardest in the last eight prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: this is public since August. What is not visible is a revenue bar consistent with it. FY27 revenue estimates near $5.6-5.7B imply about +8% on a FY26 at about $5.2B, which needs either Agile Defense included or a sharp organic re-acceleration that 0.5x book-to-bill does not support. If the bar is the ex-Agile organic one, it is too high.
findings.independence: The Leidos Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15861762119343104) on federal decision delays is a different company but the same macro procurement environment, so it is a proxy. The Q3 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001032220/000103222026000033/mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm) carries the same revenue numbers and is the same company's disclosure.

findings.finding: Agile Defense, announced 2026-10-19 and expected to close in Q1 FY27: about $450M calendar-2026 revenue at a 12-15% adj EBITDA margin (about $54-68M EBITDA), bought for $660M cash (about 10-12x) plus a $50M earnout. Pro forma net leverage goes to 2.2-2.3x from 1.7x. If the first FY27 guide includes it, it adds roughly $300-400M of revenue (about +6-8%). My own arithmetic, not a company figure: it adds about $0.15-0.25 of adj EPS, because MMS's adj EPS excludes intangible amortization and the about $40M of financing interest is below the EBITDA. That could make a headline FY27 revenue guide look like growth even with flat organic revenue. On financing: the money buys revenue, so this is a positive or a zero, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock moved -0.39% on 2026-10-20, the deal-announcement session. No prior print carried an acquisition-inclusive guide in the last eight.
findings.why_not_priced: With two analysts and no disclosed accretion or multiple, it is unclear whether FY27 estimates include the deal. A FY27 revenue bar near $5.6B is consistent with either view. If the deal were in the price, published FY27 EPS would have moved up by about $0.2 after 2026-10-20, and no update is visible.
findings.independence: The SEC 8-K of 2026-10-20 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1032220/000103222026000038/mms-20261019.htm) gives the leverage ratios and the closing timing. It is a different document from the trade-press revenue and margin figures.

findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, because it sits inside the company's own guide. The only unpriced piece is the small gap between the consensus and the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: The company guide is in the Q3 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001032220/000103222026000033/mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm), a different source from the consensus.

findings.finding: Capital return: the full $400M buyback authorization was unused at June 30, and MMS has bought back about 14% of its shares since the start of FY25. The $660M cash deal takes leverage to 2.2-2.3x, inside the 2-3x target. That makes a slower FY27 buyback likely, which reduces share-count support for FY27 EPS against a bar that may assume continued repurchases. This is an inference; the company has said nothing about FY27 buyback pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $400M authorization refresh came with the 2026-05-07 print, which moved +4.24% alongside a raised EPS outlook. The buyback has not been isolated as a driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates that model FY27 share count off the FY25-26 buyback pace would not reflect a pause for M&A deleveraging. With no visible estimate revision, it is unclear.
findings.independence: The Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504) gives the 14% repurchased and the M&A priority. It is the same company's disclosures, so this is not independent.

findings.finding: Medicaid work requirements, the US Services upside: the 2027-01-01 start stands, with semiannual redeterminations for about 21M expansion enrollees. On 2026-10-29 the D. Mass. court (Massachusetts v. Oz) vacated CMS's added work-related functional test for medical frailty in the plaintiff states. CMS said on 2026-11-03 it will appeal, and further guidance is due in November, so states' operational designs stay provisional. On the Q3 call MMS had said state customer discussions were progressing 'more slowly than expected'. Expect a cautious FY27 contribution from this line: the upside is real but late and hard to quantify in a guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Medicaid redetermination cycle drove FY24-25 US Services growth. No print in the last eight turned on work-requirement wins specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: The court ruling (2026-10-29) and the CMS appeal (2026-11-03) came after MMS last spoke. Narrowing the frailty test could reduce exemption-assessment work in the plaintiff states while keeping the core eligibility-verification volume. It is net ambiguous, and nobody has modelled it for MMS.
findings.independence: The MMS Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504) describes slower state discussions and the 2027-01-01 timing. It is a separate document from the HMA blog.

outside_window.finding: The VA MDE recompete award is expected April-May 2027 with work starting 2027-07-01. Leidos sees an 'upside case' for more work share for itself, which is a relative share risk for MMS/VES. The final RFP was expected in November 2026 and was not yet issued as of 2026-11-03.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew, so the only market statement is the tape. The stock is up about 14% since the August print and +5% over 20 days, which looks like the market pricing a temporary VA pause. lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): the FY27 bar has one unverified source plus stale tables, so the Leidos guidance finding was capped from -2.0 to -1.5.

Lesson 5 (documents beat inference) and the core rule for partly priced facts: the book-to-bill finding is a company document but public since August, so -1.0 became -0.7. The Agile accretion finding rests on my own arithmetic, so +1.0 became +0.8. The buyback inference went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, 2 analysts) and a first FY27 guide: abs_move_pct raised from 8.5 to 9.0.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the post-August rally cuts against the negative lean, so p_up moved from 44 to 45.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the Agile financing is signed as buying revenue (a positive or a zero), not distress. That was unchanged from the draft.
